To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the prevalence of LBW in Vietnam in the year 2010 was 5.8%; 2) the prevalence of preterm birth was 6.7%; and 3) the prevalence of clinically significant symptoms of ACMDs during the third trimesters of pregnancy was 9.1%.

(i) the prevalence of antenatal depression and anxiety symptoms is high in rural Vietnam; and, (ii) these symptoms are associated with adverse perinatal outcomes (preterm birth and low‐birth weight), independent of other known risk factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between maternal mental health and infant health.
the relationship between the symptoms of antenateral common mental disorders and low birth weight.
the relationship between maternal mental health and birth outcomes, including preterm birth, low birthweight, and small for gestational age.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence does support a causal association between maternal mental disorders and adverse birth outcomes.

the use of antenatal corticosteroids in women who have preterm labor or are at risk of preterm delivery does not appear to increase the risk of maternal or neonatal adverse effects, including death, infection, or neurologic impairment.
there is a positive association between antenatal common symptoms of mental disorders and LBW.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prevalence of antenatal mental disorders was high in this semi‐rural setting, and was associated with preterm birth and LBW.
the results of this study indicate that the risk of antenatal mental disorders is increased among women who are pregnant with a low birth weight baby.

we have demonstrated the importance of the role of mental health and wellbeing in the lives of women and their families, and that the provision of mental health services is an important component of the overall health system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the association between antenatal depression and low birth weight is not causal.
there is a need for more rigorous studies to examine the association of LBW with ACMDs, and to identify the underlying mechanisms that link the two.
the risk of preterm birth is significantly increased by a history of preterm birth, and that this risk increases with the number of previous preterm births.
